title: Array Bounds
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-001 Array Bounds. Accessing arrays or buffers without checking the index or length can read or write outside allocated storage. Out-of-bounds access can cause crashes, data corruption, or memory-safety issues in C/C++ and unexpected exceptions in managed languages. buf[index] used without confirming 0 <= index < length Validate indexes against the actual allocated or logical length before access. Prefer safer APIs and bounded copies. High when bounds are missing on attacker-influenced indexes; Medium when bounds are unclear. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Pointer / Null Validation
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-002 Pointer / Null Validation. Pointers, references, and nullable objects should be validated before dereference or method calls. Null or invalid pointer use can crash embedded software, cause undefined behavior, or throw NullPointerException / TypeError. ptr->field without checking ptr != NULL; obj.method() without null checks Check pointers/objects before use. Initialize pointers. Document ownership. In Java/Python, handle None/null explicitly. High for unchecked dereference of possibly null pointers; Medium for nullable objects with unclear lifetime. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Variable Initialization
languages: C, C++, Java
text: SEC-003 Variable Initialization. Variables, buffers, and pointers should be initialized before they are read. Uninitialized memory can leak leftover data, produce non-deterministic behavior, or fail safety-related checks. int x; used in a condition before assignment Initialize at declaration. Zero buffers. Avoid reading locals before assignment. Educational MISRA-oriented guidance recommends definite assignment before use. High in C/C++ safety-critical paths; Medium otherwise. C, C++, Java

title: Integer Overflow and Range
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-004 Integer Overflow and Range. Arithmetic on integers can wrap, overflow, or produce invalid indexes and sizes. Overflow can bypass size checks, allocate too little memory, or produce incorrect control decisions in ECU software. len + offset used as an allocation size without overflow checks Check ranges before arithmetic. Use wider types or saturating/checked operations where available. Validate against documented min/max. High when overflow can affect buffers or safety decisions; Medium for general arithmetic. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Unsafe Buffer Operations
languages: C, C++
text: SEC-005 Unsafe Buffer Operations. Unbounded string and memory copy functions can overflow destination buffers. Classic buffer overflows remain a common reliability and security issue in C/C++. strcpy, strcat, sprintf, gets, scanf("%s") Use bounded APIs (strncpy/strlcpy/snprintf/memcpy_s where approved). Always pass destination size. Avoid gets(). High for unbounded copies of untrusted or unbounded input. C, C++

title: Resource Management
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-006 Resource Management. Files, sockets, memory, mutexes, and other resources must be acquired and released on all paths. Leaks can exhaust ECU resources. Double-free and use-after-free cause undefined behavior. malloc without matching free; open() without close; new without delete Pair acquire/release. Use RAII, try-with-resources, or context managers. Check allocation results. Medium to High depending on resource criticality and error paths. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Input Validation
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-007 Input Validation. External input (network, sensors, user data, files, APIs) must be validated for type, length, range, and encoding. Unvalidated input can drive injection, overflow, logic errors, and unsafe control flow. Using request data directly as a filename, SQL fragment, command, or array index Validate at trust boundaries. Use allow-lists. Reject unexpected values. Do not rely only on client-side checks. High when input influences commands, queries, paths, or memory sizes. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Global State
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-008 Global State. Excessive mutable global or static state makes behavior harder to reason about and review. Hidden coupling can cause race conditions, unexpected side effects, and reuse defects across modules. Many non-const globals modified from multiple functions Limit globals. Prefer explicit parameters and encapsulated modules. Protect shared state if concurrency exists. Low to Medium; raise severity if globals store secrets or safety-critical values. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Control Flow
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-009 Control Flow. Complex, unreachable, or dangerous control flow (goto, empty catch, always-true conditions) hides defects. Reviewers may miss missing error paths. Educational MISRA-oriented guidance discourages unstructured jumps. goto error; empty catch {}; if (true) { ... } Prefer structured control flow. Handle errors explicitly. Avoid dead branches and swallowed exceptions. Medium for swallowed errors; Low for style-only complexity unless safety-related. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Input Size Assumptions
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-010 Input Size Assumptions. Code should not assume a fixed maximum size for external data. Truncation or overflow occurs when real-world payloads exceed assumed sizes. Copying a network payload into a 64-byte stack buffer without checking length Enforce documented maximums. Reject oversized input. Size buffers from validated lengths, not from trust. High when size is attacker-controlled; Medium when limits are undocumented. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Error Handling
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-011 Error Handling. Failed calls, I/O errors, and invalid states should be detected and handled. Ignoring return values can leave systems in unsafe or partially initialized states. Ignoring malloc NULL; ignoring fread return; empty catch Check return codes. Define fail-safe behavior. Do not continue as if success occurred. Medium to High depending on the failed operation. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Hardcoded Secrets
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-012 Hardcoded Secrets. Passwords, API keys, tokens, and certificates must not be embedded in source code. Source repositories, logs, and binaries can leak credentials used against production systems. api_key = "sk-live-..." or password = "admin123" Use secrets management or environment variables outside source. Rotate if secrets were committed. Never print secrets. High for production-looking credentials; Medium for obvious placeholders still stored in code. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Unsafe Command Execution
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-013 Unsafe Command Execution. Building OS commands from untrusted data can allow command injection. Attackers may execute unintended programs on the host or build environment. os.system(user); subprocess(..., shell=True); Runtime.exec(userInput) Avoid shells. Use fixed executables with argument arrays. Validate and allow-list arguments. High when user or external data reaches a shell or exec API. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Unsafe Deserialization
languages: Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++
text: SEC-014 Unsafe Deserialization. Deserializing untrusted data can instantiate unexpected objects or execute logic. Pickle, YAML load, Java ObjectInputStream, and similar APIs can lead to remote code execution or integrity loss. pickle.loads(data); new ObjectInputStream(in).readObject(); yaml.load(untrusted) Prefer safe formats (JSON with schema). Use safe loaders. Authenticate and validate payloads. High for untrusted streams; Medium when source is unclear. Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++

title: Injection Risks
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-015 Injection Risks. Untrusted data concatenated into SQL, HTML, logs, or interpreters can change meaning. Injection can alter queries, execute scripts in browsers, or poison logs. "SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=" + user; element.innerHTML = user; eval(user) Parameterized queries. Context-appropriate encoding. Avoid eval and innerHTML with untrusted data. High for SQL/command/HTML injection indicators. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Authentication / Authorization Checks
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-016 Authentication / Authorization Checks. Privileged operations should verify identity and permissions. Missing checks can expose diagnostic, configuration, or safety interfaces. Admin API handler with no auth check Deny by default. Check authorization server-side. Do not rely only on hidden URLs. High when privileged actions appear unchecked; Medium when checks are incomplete. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Sensitive Data Handling
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-017 Sensitive Data Handling. Secrets, PII, keys, and diagnostic dumps should be minimized, protected, and not logged. Logs and crash dumps are frequently copied outside the original trust boundary. logging.info("password=%s", password) Redact secrets. Encrypt sensitive stores. Limit retention. Avoid writing secrets to traces. High when secrets are logged or stored in plaintext; Medium for other sensitive fields. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Exception Handling
languages: Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++
text: SEC-018 Exception Handling. Exceptions and errors should not be ignored or overly broad. Empty catch blocks hide faults. Catching Exception/BaseException can swallow safety-relevant failures. except: pass; catch (Exception e) {} Catch specific exceptions. Log safely. Recover or fail closed according to policy. Medium typically; High if safety or security errors are swallowed. Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++

title: Logging and Information Exposure
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-019 Logging and Information Exposure. Logs should not include secrets, full payloads, or internal paths that aid attackers. Verbose logs can leak credentials, tokens, and architecture details. console.log(request.headers.authorization) Log identifiers, not secrets. Apply log levels. Review diagnostic builds separately. Medium to High depending on data sensitivity. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Dependency / API Security
languages: C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript
text: SEC-020 Dependency / API Security. Third-party APIs and dynamic code loading can introduce trust and supply-chain risk. Unpinned dependencies, insecure TLS usage, or dynamic eval of remote scripts expand the attack surface. fetch("http://...") without TLS; eval of remote content; disabling certificate checks Pin approved versions. Use TLS. Avoid dynamic code from the network. Review new APIs. Medium to High depending on trust of the dependency or endpoint. C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript

title: Educational MISRA-oriented guidance — language subset and undefined behavior
languages: C, C++
text: MISRA-EDU-001 Educational MISRA-oriented guidance — language subset and undefined behavior. Educational MISRA-oriented guidance encourages a safer C/C++ subset, avoiding undefined behavior, implicit conversions, and unbounded operations. This project does not perform official MISRA compliance checking. Automotive and embedded teams often use MISRA as a quality framework. Educational reminders help reviewers, but certification requires qualified processes and tools. Implicit mixed signed/unsigned arithmetic; unbounded strcpy; use of dynamic features where a simpler subset is required Follow the organization's approved coding standard. Use certified analyzers for compliance evidence. Treat this assistant as educational support only. Informational to Medium unless paired with a concrete unsafe pattern. C, C++

title: Educational MISRA-oriented guidance — mandatory error checking
languages: C, C++
text: MISRA-EDU-002 Educational MISRA-oriented guidance — mandatory error checking. Educational MISRA-oriented guidance emphasizes checking return values, avoiding silent failures, and keeping control flow structured. Unchecked failures in ECU software can leave actuators or diagnostics in an undefined state. Ignoring the result of a communication or memory allocation call Handle every relevant error path. Prefer explicit status codes. Document fail-safe behavior. Medium to High on safety-relevant paths. C, C++
